title: Cohomology of a derived base-change map
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, and $g':X'\to X$. Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$, placed in degree zero in the bounded below derived category. For $q\in\mathbf Z$, under the canonical identifications
$$
\mathcal H^q(g^{-1}Rf_*F)\cong g^{-1}R^qf_*F,\qquad
\mathcal H^q(Rf'_*g'^{-1}F)=R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F,
$$
from [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], the map $\mathcal H^q(\Ex_{\square,F})$ of the derived exchange [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is the usual higher-direct-image base-change map
$$
g^{-1}R^qf_*F\longrightarrow R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F.
$$
Here the usual map is the injective-resolution construction extending the underived exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]: apply that exchange termwise to a resolution of $F$, compare its $g'^{-1}$-pullback with a resolution on $X'$, and take degree-$q$ cohomology. For negative $q$ both higher direct images are zero. All coefficients in this statement are abelian groups.

proof.text: Choose a K-injective resolution $F[0]\to I$ and a K-injective resolution $j:g'^{-1}I\to J$, using [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist] with $R=\mathbf Z$, the abelian-sheaf convention of [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $g'^{-1}(F[0])\to g'^{-1}I$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its degree-$r$ cohomology is $g'^{-1}$ applied to the isomorphism on degree-$r$ cohomology of $F[0]\to I$. Thus the composite $g'^{-1}F[0]\to J$ resolves $g'^{-1}F[0]$. No injectivity of $g'^{-1}I$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise] to $K=F[0]$, the resolution $I$ and $j$. It supplies a chain map
$$e=f'_*(j)\circ\Ex^0_{\square,I}:g^{-1}f_*I\longrightarrow f'_*J,$$
and the precise equation $\Ex_{\square,F}\circ\sigma_{\rm src}=\sigma_{\rm tgt}\circ Q(e)$ under its canonical resolution identifications. Consequently applying the functor $\mathcal H^q$ to this equation computes the map in the item by $H^q(e)$ under $H^q(\sigma_{\rm src})$ and $H^q(\sigma_{\rm tgt})$.

proof.text:
Identify the source of $H^q(e)$ with $g^{-1}R^qf_*F$. Indeed [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] makes $g^{-1}$ exact, and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives the cycle-and-boundary comparison
$$H^q(g^{-1}f_*I)\cong g^{-1}H^q(f_*I)=g^{-1}R^qf_*F.$$
The last equality is the resolution computation in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The same definition, using the resolution of $g'^{-1}F$ in step 1, identifies $H^q(f'_*J)$ with $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F$. These are the identifications in the statement, since the derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] is represented by termwise inverse image and its comparison is natural in complexes. For completeness, the negative-degree assertion follows from [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] with $n=0$, separately for $F[0]$ and $g'^{-1}F[0]$. Both have zero cohomology below zero, so each has a representative consisting of injective sheaves and zero terms below zero. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] their derived direct images are computed by applying the additive direct-image functor to these representatives. Those complexes are again zero below zero, hence their negative cohomology vanishes.

proof.text: Write out the resulting map. In degree $q$, a local section $a$ of the cycle subsheaf of $g^{-1}f_*I$ maps to $f'_*(j^q)(\Ex^0_{\square,I^q}(a))$; the chain-map equation implies this is a cycle and sends every boundary to a boundary. The map therefore factors through the cokernel of the boundary-subsheaf inclusion into the cycle subsheaf, which is the cohomology sheaf. Its formula on locally represented classes is $[a]\mapsto[f'_*(j^q)(\Ex^0_{\square,I^q}(a))]$. This is a statement about the quotient sheaf; it does not assert that every section of cohomology has a global cycle representative. Here [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] says that $\Ex^0$ restricts sections along $X'\times_{Y'}V\to X\times_YW$, followed by sheafification. Thus this quotient map is exactly the usual resolution recipe stated above: restrict by the underived exchange and then compare resolutions. Together with steps 2 and 3 this proves the asserted equality, without substituting the sheaf $\mathcal H^q(F)$ for $F$. The formula is valid in all degrees; for $q<0$ the zero higher direct images give the unique zero-to-zero map.
